question.leadin: The final holder of this title was Tokugawa Yoshinobu.
question.text: Prior to an 1868 restoration of imperial rule, what title was held by military rulers of Japan?
question.clue: Two successive dynasties in this position supported the illegitimate Northern Court.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about emperors of Japan.
swap.text: This man has the distinction of maintaining the longest reign of any Japanese emperor. He is more famously known for overseeing the Japanese surrender during World War II.
swap.clue: The empowerment of this man was the state goal of the League of Blood, while the year of his ascension saw a financial crisis triggered by the devaluation of Earthquake Bonds, leading to the rise of conglomerate control of the economy.

question.leadin: Saigo Takamori was an influential member of this class.
question.text: Name this class of warrior nobility from feudal Japan. Members of this class traditionally carried both a long katana and a shorter sword.
question.clue: Members of this group could find a job by embarking on a type of pilgrimage called musha shugyo, and their only goal should be "to grasp the long and the short swords and to die".

swap.leadin: The busiest one of these locations in the United States is Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International.
swap.text: Name these locations, such as O'Hare International. These locations often require extensive security checks before a traveller is allowed near a runway.
swap.clue: After several Montoneros and Peronists gathered at one of these places, right-wing snipers shot into the crowd during the Ezeiza massacre.

question.text: Before Tokugawa and Toyotomi, this victor at Okehazama was the first of Japan's unifiers, helping end the Warring-States period. He committed suicide at Honno-ji temple in Kyoto.
question.clue: This man was forced to commit seppuku after being betrayed by Akechi Mitsuhide at Honno-ji.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the usage of planes during World War II.
swap.text: The Mitsubishi Zero which was developed in this country possessed a notoriously thin aluminum skin which allowed it to be agile at the cost of protection. This country encouraged kamikaze pilots three years after it bombed Pearl Harbor.
swap.clue: Its navy staged a successful attack in the Battle of Port Arthur during a conflict ended by negotiations in Maine with a rival country's diplomat Sergei Witte.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Hojo clan.
question.text: The Hojo were the effective rulers during this shogunate named for a city that's today famous for a large Buddha statue. This shogunate took power after the Heian period.
question.clue: Before a major battle one leader of this polity meditated to find the source of cowardice in himself, and one conflict during it occurred when the cloistered emperor Go-Toba attempted to take the throne.

swap.leadin: During this period, emperors who retired to monasteries retained power in the system of cloistered rule.
swap.text: Name this period that succeeded the Nara Period. This period came to an end with the Genpei War.
swap.clue: The Fujiwara clan held de facto power during this period, which was ended by the Genpei ] War and began when Emperor Kanmu moved the capital to Kyoto.

question.text: The Restoration began in 1868 with the issuance of this document which promised legislatures, class unification, an end to "evil customs of the past," and the seeking of knowledge.
question.answerHtml: Charter Oath [or Imperial Oath Of Five Articles; or Gokajo No Goseimon]
question.clue: This document was created when Emperor Meiji took power in 1868. It laid out Meiji's goals for Westernization, and can be considered the first constitution of modern-day Japan.

swap.leadin: During this era, a period of economic expansion and the flourishing of the arts took place in its Genroku Period.
swap.text: Identify this government that was ended by an era of rapid industrialization called the Meiji restoration. Ieyasu was its first leader.
swap.answerHtml: Tokugawa Shogunate [or Tokugawa Period; or Edo Period; or Tokugawa Bafuku; or Edo Bafuku]
swap.clue: Supporters of this dynasty lost at the Battle of Hakodate after starting the Ezo Republic during the Boshin War.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the battle of Sekigahara.
question.text: This victor at Sekigahara established a namesake shogunate that lasted into the nineteenth century.
question.clue: As head of the Eastern Army, this man defeated the forces of Ishida Mitsunari at the Battle of Sekigahara.

swap.text: Ieyasu, the commander of the Eastern Army at Sekigahara became shogun in 1603, established this clan of his as rulers of Japan during the Edo Period.
swap.clue: One leader with this surname was defeated by Takeda Shingen, but later won a major battle at Nagashino, in alliance with a man who was betrayed and killed by Akechi Mitsuhide, Oda Nobunaga.

question.text: This research group under the Kwantung Army committed some of the greatest Japanese crimes against humanity during the war. It was commanded by Shiro Ishii, who was pardoned by the United States after the war in exchange for his data.
question.answerHtml: Unit 731 [accept Nana-san-ichi Butai; accept Epidemic Prevention and Water Purification Department of the Kwantung Army; accept Kantogun Boeki Kyusuibu Honbu]
question.clue: This group within the Epidemic Prevention and Purification Department. A guy actually named Colonel Sanders brought it to the attention of Douglas MacArthur, who pardoned its leader in exchange for scientific data.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about famous war photographers.
swap.text: Joe Rosenthal took an iconic image of five marines raising a flag on this Pacific Island during World War II. Clint Eastwood directed a film told from the Japanese perspective called Letters from This place.
swap.clue: The February to March 1945 struggle for this island at Meatgrinder Hill and Mount Suribachi ended with a certain flag-raising.

question.leadin: The final battle in this war saw the sinking of the ship carrying the Emperor Antoku, and this war is detailed in the Tale of the Heike.
question.text: Name this 12th century civil war in Japan fought between the Taira and Minamoto clans, which ended at the naval battle of Dan-no-Ura
question.clue: Chronicled in the Azuma kagami, the first major battle of this conflict ended with Yorimasa's death by seppuku after he failed to defend Prince Mochihito; that was the battle of the Uji river.

swap.leadin: Ka'en jars, with tops that resemble flames, were principally produced during the middle of this period.
swap.text: Name this period, which gets its name from using rope to make marks on pottery. The Yayoi culture succeeded this period.
swap.clue: This period's namesake hunter-gatherers were supplanted by the agricultural Yayoi ] people.

question.leadin: Unlike the Gishi Wajinden, this chronicle makes little mention of Empress Himiko, a semi-mythical shaman queen who established relations with Cao Wei ("tsao way").
question.text: Name this work, which was completed eight years after the Kojiki and chronicles national myths and history up to the 8th century.
question.clue: This set of chronicles, the most comprehensive text available for scholarship on Ancient Japan. It was completed under the supervision of Prince Toneri and presented to Empress Gensho in the year 720.

swap.leadin: Emperor Kotoku implemented this set of policies, which included the abolition of private landholding and a tax based on population instead of land use.
swap.text: Name this 645 A.D. set of centralizing reforms inspired by Tang Dynasty China, which brought Japan under the control of the imperial court.
swap.answerHtml: Taika Reforms [or Taika no Kaishin; or Great Reformation of the Taika Era]
swap.clue: The Asuka period ended with this set of reforms promulgated by the Kotoku Emperor which centralized power and introduced reorganization based on Tang Chinese lines.

question.text: The Tokugawa shogun Iemitsu instituted this system, which required each of the daimyo to spend a part of the year in Edo and leave family members as hostages in order to prevent rebellion.

swap.leadin: Frank Capra used this document as evidence in his propaganda film Why We Fight.
swap.text: Name this probably fictitious document which called for conquest of Manchuria and China as the path to Japanese dominance in East Asia.
swap.clue: James Cagney starred in a film based on a fictional scenario in which this document is smuggled to the United States, Blood on the Sun, and it is heavily featured in Frank Capra's Why We Fight.
